Reconstruct the visible indoor scene from one RGB photograph using SceneAct and Blender.
Infer geometry and a camera matching the reference viewpoint, perspective and framing.
Use separate 3D meshes for architecture, furniture and visible objects, preserving colors,
proportions, placement, occlusions and materials. Do not use the reference as a texture,
background or projected image. No ground-truth calibration or other views are available.

Return a complete, runnable Python program inside one ```python code block. Each execution
starts in a fresh Blender process. Programs can use numpy, sceneact and bpy. Use SceneAct
for geometry and relationships; bpy may customize lighting, materials and camera settings.
Do not render or save files in the program: the fixed runner saves and renders once after
execution, using your active camera. Do not access external files, network or other models.
When satisfied after inspecting a rendering, reply exactly DONE. The last successful build
is submitted automatically unless you return SELECT n for a successful rendered step listed
by the controller. Budget includes all planning, corrections and review calls. Maximum:
5 fresh CLI sessions, 3 Blender executions and 1200 seconds. Actual runtime counters govern.
No active diagnostic renders, isolated views, camera sweeps or scale sweeps are permitted.

Shared reconstruction procedure:
1. Before detailed modeling, identify the principal architectural lines, visible object
silhouettes, floor contacts, cropped foreground objects and near/far overlap order. Record
about six normalized image anchors in concise source comments, labeled visual estimates.
Use a consistent arbitrary world scale; a single photograph does not reveal metric scale.
Create separate parameter sections for camera, architecture, object dimensions/poses,
materials and lighting. Build a complete but economical scene on the first execution.
2. Fit camera orientation using architectural convergence and visible top/side faces; fit
framing using image margins and anchors at different depths. A focal-length change affects
many projected objects; an object-scale change affects a local silhouette and its contacts.
Camera translation changes relative near/far size. Do not compensate for a global framing
error by independently enlarging many objects. These are geometric heuristics, not proof of
which parameter is wrong. Keep alternative explanations explicit when evidence is ambiguous.
3. Keep a visible-object inventory. An object absent from the render may be missing from the
graph, overwritten by a repeated include key, outside the frame, or occluded. Inspect the
source and depth ordering before adding duplicates or moving it. Preserve partial objects
at image boundaries. Do not remove an evidenced object merely to improve a silhouette.
4. Group each semantic object under an Asset with its own supports, surfaces and trim as
named children. Assemble repeated objects with unique keys within each parent. Include all
parts before moving or resizing the parent. Represent supports with shared dimensions,
explicit anchors or appropriate acyclic bindings. Check feet against the floor and objects
against their actual supporting surfaces. AABB proximity/overlap is only approximate and
can be intentional within a constructed shape; it is not true contact or collision truth.
5. Spend complexity on silhouette, relative depth, large color regions and visible supports
before subpixel pattern geometry. Use moderate primitive counts and short tube paths.
Prefer supported SceneAct constructions for all visible geometry so the editable hierarchy
contains the complete object. Keep independent semantic objects separate; do not fuse the
whole scene. Do not optimize names or group structure to manipulate evaluator targeting.
6. After each successful render, compare the same anchors and visible inventory. Record the
largest discrepancies and a bounded planned change. Correct camera/layout before decorative
detail when multiple anchors disagree. Once architecture agrees, prefer local object edits.
Avoid changing camera, object scale and lighting together without an explicit need. A single
score difference cannot establish causality. Never claim measured scores not supplied.
7. Preserve editability during every revision: nonempty finite meshes, meaningful parents,
local material isolation, and complete composite movement. A functional pass certifies only
the prescribed operation on its selected target, not semantic completeness or correct 3D.
Use any supplied fixed regression failures to prioritize repairs; missing results are unknown.
Do not run extra regression renders or change fixed acceptance criteria.

Source audit before execution:
- All dimensions/radii must be finite and positive. fillet_box requires
  0 < radius <= min(size)/2, including thin slabs. Use a smaller radius or another supported
  construction when the desired rounding exceeds thickness; never silently enlarge the slab.
- Rod endpoints must differ. Consecutive sweep_tube points must differ.
- include replaces an existing child with the same key. Loops and helper functions must
  generate unique per-parent keys. Store the node returned by include when ownership matters.
- realize clears Blender. Set camera, lights, world and material customization afterward.
  bpy.context.scene.world may be None: create bpy.data.worlds.new(...) and assign it before
  setting use_nodes, color or Background inputs. Do not assume a default World survives.
- Named SceneAct include slots become EMPTY parents; emitted meshes may be named Box, Rod
  or Ball. For local bpy material work, find the exact named parent, recursively traverse its
  descendants and select MESH objects. Assert that the intended set is nonempty. Do not
  search only mesh names for an Asset label. Materials are cached by finish and may be shared;
  copy a material into the target slot before a local shader change. Avoid broad color-based
  or global material edits for a local request. Preserve non-target materials and geometry.
- Use the reference aspect ratio. Do not change fixed runner settings or evaluator behavior.
- An error or missing render is an output failure. Diagnose its log, not imaginary pixels.
  Repair analogous API mistakes in the same program before spending another execution.

SceneAct API (all coordinates in a world frame with Z up; angles in degrees):
from sceneact import *
Scene(name='Scene'), Asset(name='Asset'), Part(name, *nodes)
parent.include(name, node) attaches an asset/part while preserving its world position.
parent.members[name] retrieves a child; parent.remove(name) detaches it.
node.clone() returns an independent subtree. scene.replicate(name, new_name) duplicates an asset.
box(size=(x,y,z), center=(x,y,z), color=(r,g,b), opacity=1)
ball(radius, center=(0,0,0), color=(1,1,1), opacity=1)
rod(radius, start=(x,y,z), end=(x,y,z), color=(r,g,b))
rod(radius, length=h, center=(0,0,0), axis='+z', color=(r,g,b))
fillet_box(size=(x,y,z), radius=r, center=(0,0,0), color=(r,g,b))
sweep_tube(points=[(x,y,z), ...], radius=.03, color=(r,g,b))
assemble(nodes, name='Assembly') groups shapes without merging their meshes.
fuse(*nodes), subtract(base,*cutters), overlap(*nodes), exclusive(left,right) construct solids.
node.move(offset), node.turn(axis, degrees, pivot=None), node.resize(factors, pivot=None)
modify a node and its descendants. node.turn(euler=(rx,ry,rz)) applies X, then Y, then Z.
Default rotation/scale pivot is the geometry's world-space bounding-box center.
shifted(node, offset), turned(node, axis, degrees, pivot=None, euler=None),
resized(node, factors, pivot=None) perform the same operations on independent copies.
node.paint(color, opacity=1) applies color to the subtree; node.rgba reads its finish.
node.centroid, node.dimensions, node.limits give AABB center, size, (minimum,maximum).
node.landmark('top'), node.landmark('front_left_bottom') return bounding-box anchors.
node.extreme(direction) returns a support point; projected_span(node,direction) returns bounds
along a unit direction; projected_width(node,direction) returns their difference.
snap(node, target, source_anchor='center', target_anchor=None, offset=(0,0,0)) returns a copy.
For an Asset target, omitted target_anchor uses source_anchor. For a world point, omit
 target_anchor. For bottom-on-top placement, pass both anchor names explicitly.
abut(node, target, axis='+z', gap=0) places a copy after a target boundary.
center_on(node, target, axes=('x','y','z')) aligns selected center coordinates.
offset_at(node, reference, offsets) positions selected coordinates; None preserves a coordinate.
repeat_line(nodes, axis='+x', spacing=1) uses equal center spacing, keeping the first fixed.
pile(nodes, axis='+z', gap=0) spaces bounding surfaces, keeping the first fixed.
lattice(nodes, rows=None, columns=None, spacing=(1,1), plane='xy', center=(0,0,0), order='row-major')
orbit(nodes, radius, axis='+z', center=(0,0,0), start=0, sweep=360, orient=False, rotation_offset=0)
Layout functions return assemblies of independent copies.
scene.bind(source,target,source_anchor='center',target_anchor='center',offset=(0,0,0))
registers a persistent relation between scene members; scene.settle() updates dependencies.
Binding endpoints must belong to the scene, cannot be ancestor/descendant, and must not form
cycles. Pass explicit bottom/top anchors when registering a support relation.
realize(scene) settles constraints and creates Blender geometry, clearing Blender first.
set_view(position,target,lens=35,sensor=36,shift=(0,0)) creates the active camera.
area_emitter(position,power=500,size=5,target=(0,0,0),color=(1,1,1)) creates an area light.
Call realize before setting the camera and lighting. Estimate the input viewpoint yourself.

Example:
from sceneact import *
scene = Scene()
table = Asset('table')
table.include('top', box((1.4,.8,.08), center=(0,0,.75), color=(.4,.2,.1)))
for x in (-.6,.6):
    for y in (-.3,.3):
        table.include(f'leg_{x}_{y}', box((.07,.07,.7), center=(x,y,.35)))
scene.include('table', table)
scene.include('floor', box((6,6,.1), center=(0,0,-.05), color=(.6,.6,.6)))
realize(scene)
set_view((3,-4,2), (0,0,.7), lens=40)
area_emitter((0,-2,4), power=1000)

```python
from sceneact import *
import bpy
import math

# Visual estimates, normalized image anchors:
# Main column: (.72,.84) at floor, (.77,.02) at ceiling.
# Front bunk upright: (.39,.69); upper mattress front edge: (.25,.44).
# Blue lockers: (.10,.59); rear steel lockers: (.49,.46).
# Red wall fitting: (.81,.55); rear chair contact: (.48,.66).
# Foreground bench enters at (.92,.87); rear floor boundary near (.57,.67).
# Arbitrary scale; inferred narrow shipboard compartment. Camera distance and
# bunk depth are uncertain. Longitudinal beams and bunks establish depth.

# CAMERA
CAM_POS = (0.05, -4.2, 1.66)
CAM_TARGET = (0.04, 3.0, 1.69)
LENS = 26

# ARCHITECTURE
ROOM_W, ROOM_D, ROOM_H = 4.4, 9.2, 3.55
FLOOR = (0.30, 0.105, 0.060)
WALL = (0.62, 0.63, 0.52)
CREAM = (0.76, 0.75, 0.60)
IRON = (0.075, 0.095, 0.085)
STEEL = (0.39, 0.43, 0.40)
BLUE = (0.085, 0.16, 0.19)
BED = (0.66, 0.68, 0.59)
WOOD = (0.40, 0.19, 0.085)

# OBJECT DIMENSIONS / POSES
BUNK_X = -1.35
BUNK_Y = 1.48
BUNK_W, BUNK_L = 1.28, 3.25
BUNK_LEVELS = (0.48, 1.12, 1.76)
POLE = (0.77, -1.45)
scene = Scene('Shipboard sleeping and machinery compartment')

def put(parent, name, size, center, color):
    return parent.include(name, box(size=size, center=center, color=color))

def tube(parent, name, a, b, radius=.022, color=IRON):
    return parent.include(name, rod(radius=radius, start=a, end=b, color=color))

architecture = Asset('Compartment shell')
put(architecture, 'painted plank floor', (4.4, 9.2, .12), (0, 1.1, -.06), FLOOR)
put(architecture, 'port bulkhead', (.12, 9.2, 3.55), (-2.2, 1.1, 1.775), WALL)
put(architecture, 'rear bulkhead', (4.4, .14, 3.55), (0, 5.65, 1.775), CREAM)
put(architecture, 'starboard bulkhead', (.12, 9.2, 3.55), (2.2, 1.1, 1.775), CREAM)
put(architecture, 'overhead deck', (4.4, 9.2, .15), (0, 1.1, 3.60), (.31,.29,.23))
put(architecture, 'rear red skirting', (4.4,.055,.34), (0,5.55,.17), (.32,.12,.075))
put(architecture, 'port skirting', (.04,9,.25), (-2.12,1.1,.125), WOOD)
for i in range(16):
    y = -3.3 + i*.56
    put(architecture, f'floor board seam {i}', (4.32,.009,.004), (0,y,.003), (.21,.075,.045))
for i, x in enumerate((-1.8,-.9,.0,.9,1.8)):
    put(architecture, f'ceiling longitudinal joist {i}', (.09,9,.22), (x,1.1,3.39), WOOD)
for i, y in enumerate((-2.2,-.2,2.0,4.1)):
    put(architecture, f'transverse overhead beam {i}', (4.3,.15,.28), (0,y,3.30), (.47,.27,.13))
scene.include('architecture', architecture)

column = Asset('Foreground cream and brown support column')
tube(column, 'lower brown shaft', (POLE[0],POLE[1],.04), (POLE[0],POLE[1],1.49), .105, (.34,.16,.075))
tube(column, 'upper cream shaft', (POLE[0],POLE[1],1.49), (POLE[0],POLE[1],3.53), .105, (.70,.66,.48))
tube(column, 'foot flange', (POLE[0],POLE[1],.015), (POLE[0],POLE[1],.055), .14, (.41,.25,.14))
scene.include('main support', column)

# Each bunk includes its own supported deck, mattress and edge lip.
bunks = Asset('Three tier port sleeping rack')
front_y = BUNK_Y-BUNK_L/2
back_y = BUNK_Y+BUNK_L/2
for i, x in enumerate((-1.99,-.71)):
    for j,y in enumerate((front_y, back_y)):
        tube(bunks, f'upright {i} {j}', (x,y,.04), (x,y,2.42), .027)
for k,z in enumerate(BUNK_LEVELS):
    put(bunks, f'bunk steel deck {k}', (BUNK_W,BUNK_L,.065), (BUNK_X,BUNK_Y,z-.06), IRON)
    put(bunks, f'mattress {k}', (BUNK_W-.045,BUNK_L-.06,.105), (BUNK_X,BUNK_Y,z+.025), BED)
    put(bunks, f'folded pillow {k}', (.78,.48,.14), (BUNK_X,back_y-.40,z+.14), (.76,.76,.67))
    tube(bunks, f'outer long edge {k}', (-.70,front_y,z), (-.70,back_y,z), .025, STEEL)
    tube(bunks, f'front rail {k}', (-1.99,front_y,z-.045), (-.70,front_y,z-.045), .022)
scene.include('port bunks', bunks)

# Low foreground vented metal cabinets, with separate doors and slats.
cabinets = Asset('Blue foreground ventilated lockers')
for i,y in enumerate((-.99,-.30)):
    put(cabinets, f'cabinet body {i}', (.55,.62,1.00), (-1.94,y,.65), BLUE)
    put(cabinets, f'door panel {i}', (.025,.54,.88), (-1.647,y,.65), (.12,.21,.24))
    for j in range(15):
        put(cabinets, f'vent opening {i} {j}', (.012,.40,.014), (-1.630,y,.29+j*.045), (.025,.055,.06))
    put(cabinets, f'door latch {i}', (.035,.035,.09), (-1.613,y-.19,.72), (.48,.49,.42))
put(cabinets, 'cabinet supporting ledge', (.81,1.65,.09), (-1.84,-.66,.11), (.08,.11,.09))
scene.include('blue lockers', cabinets)

# Rear steel cupboards provide the large pale silhouette behind the rack.
lockers = Asset('Rear steel storage lockers')
for i,x in enumerate((-.67,-.09,.49)):
    put(lockers, f'body {i}', (.55,.56,1.82), (x,4.42,1.05), STEEL)
    put(lockers, f'door {i}', (.515,.027,1.73), (x,4.12,1.05), (.46,.49,.45))
    for j in range(4):
        put(lockers, f'upper ventilation {i} {j}', (.26,.012,.023), (x,4.098,1.60-j*.075), (.22,.27,.25))
    put(lockers, f'latch {i}', (.035,.035,.13), (x+.18,4.073,1.05), (.15,.17,.15))
    for j,xx in enumerate((x-.20,x+.20)):
        put(lockers, f'foot {i} {j}', (.045,.42,.15), (xx,4.42,.105), IRON)
    lockers.include(f'rounded baggage {i}', ball(radius=.17, center=(x,4.44,2.01), color=(.34,.37,.31)))
scene.include('rear lockers', lockers)

# Industrial box and its exposed vertical pipework.
machine = Asset('Central dark utility machinery')
put(machine, 'housing', (.82,.72,.98), (.45,2.94,.54), (.23,.26,.22))
put(machine, 'top cover', (.89,.77,.055), (.45,2.94,1.06), (.29,.31,.26))
put(machine, 'front panel', (.72,.025,.79), (.45,2.565,.55), (.27,.29,.25))
for i,x in enumerate((.12,.75)):
    tube(machine, f'front support {i}', (x,2.64,.02), (x,2.64,.18), .035)
for i,x in enumerate((.19,.65)):
    tube(machine, f'vertical brass pipe {i}', (x,2.94,1.08), (x,2.94,2.75), .027, (.35,.31,.18))
    tube(machine, f'pipe top cross {i}', (x,2.94,2.75), (x,4.8,2.75), .027, IRON)
    machine.include(f'valve center {i}', ball(radius=.065,center=(x,2.94,1.28),color=(.35,.31,.18)))
    tube(machine, f'valve handle {i}', (x-.11,2.94,1.29),(x+.11,2.94,1.29),.014)
scene.include('utility machine', machine)

chair = Asset('Pale metal chair in rear aisle')
cx,cy=-.40,2.49
put(chair,'seat',(.46,.43,.06),(cx,cy,.49),(.47,.46,.33))
for i,x in enumerate((cx-.21,cx+.21)):
    for j,y in enumerate((cy-.18,cy+.18)):
        tube(chair,f'leg {i} {j}',(x,y,.015),(x,y,.48),.019,(.63,.62,.46))
    tube(chair,f'back upright {i}',(x,cy+.18,.46),(x,cy+.26,.96),.021,(.62,.61,.46))
put(chair,'backrest',(.43,.06,.24),(cx,cy+.23,.83),(.45,.46,.35))
scene.include('aisle chair',chair)

# Right wall fittings are carried on a short bulkhead behind the column.
wallfit = Asset('Starboard display bulkhead and fittings')
put(wallfit,'partition',(1.38,.12,3.12),(1.50,2.85,1.56),CREAM)
put(wallfit,'brown lower paint',(1.38,.018,.35),(1.50,2.777,.175),(.32,.13,.075))
put(wallfit,'dark framed notice board',(.88,.07,.92),(1.49,2.75,1.99),(.27,.28,.23))
put(wallfit,'slate board face',(.80,.015,.84),(1.49,2.707,1.99),(.25,.29,.27))
put(wallfit,'white paper notice',(.37,.012,.69),(2.02,2.70,1.51),(.78,.78,.67))
put(wallfit,'red emergency backplate',(.37,.10,.63),(1.35,2.67,1.02),(.78,.045,.022))
wallfit.include('round red top',ball(radius=.18,center=(1.35,2.65,1.30),color=(.80,.055,.025)))
put(wallfit,'emergency handle',(.12,.10,.25),(1.35,2.57,1.11),(.24,.19,.11))
wallfit.include('handle bright cap',ball(radius=.058,center=(1.35,2.51,1.32),color=(.78,.75,.57)))
for i in range(6):
    put(wallfit,f'paper text {i}',(.25,.007,.008),(2.02,2.688,1.70-i*.055),(.40,.42,.35))
scene.include('right wall fittings',wallfit)

vent = Asset('High port wall air heater')
put(vent,'pale rectangular casing',(.20,.66,.84),(-2.03,.26,2.37),(.66,.66,.54))
for i in range(7):
    put(vent,f'dark grille slit {i}',(.017,.51,.045),(-1.92,.26,2.12+i*.075),(.055,.075,.067))
put(vent,'top label',(.017,.24,.055),(-1.914,.26,2.68),(.28,.28,.23))
scene.include('port ventilation unit',vent)

# Cropped foreground benches preserve the dark boundary silhouettes.
for name,x,y,length in [('port',-1.68,-1.12,3.4),('starboard',1.55,-2.00,2.2)]:
    bench=Asset(name+' foreground bench')
    put(bench,'dark green seat',(.59,length,.08),(x,y,.45),(.045,.11,.075))
    for i,yy in enumerate((y-length/2+.18,y+length/2-.18)):
        for j,xx in enumerate((x-.23,x+.23)):
            tube(bench,f'leg {i} {j}',(xx,yy,.01),(xx,yy,.42),.025,IRON)
    scene.include(name+' bench',bench)

pipes=Asset('Overhead service pipes and hangers')
for i,x in enumerate((-1.77,-1.38,.24)):
    tube(pipes,f'long pipe {i}',(x,-2.4,2.97),(x,5.4,2.97),.034,CREAM)
for i,y in enumerate((-.9,.85,2.55,4.25)):
    tube(pipes,f'cross service {i}',(-2.1,y,3.00),(.60,y,3.00),.025,IRON)
    tube(pipes,f'hanger {i}',(-1.42,y,3.03),(-1.42,y,3.51),.018,CREAM)
pipes.include('bent pale pipe',sweep_tube(points=[(-1.9,-1.4,3.23),(-1.05,-.35,2.91),(-.85,.25,2.85),(-.85,1.4,2.85),(-.65,1.65,3.05)],radius=.043,color=CREAM))
scene.include('service pipes',pipes)

# LIGHTING: pendant fixtures are explicit editable geometry.
for i,(x,y,z,r) in enumerate(((-.65,-1.10,2.94,.29),(-.38,1.62,2.86,.18),(.10,3.50,2.84,.15))):
    lamp=Asset(f'Pendant lamp {i}')
    tube(lamp,'cord',(x,y,z+.11),(x,y,3.48),.014,IRON)
    lamp.include('metal shade',rod(radius=r,length=.075,center=(x,y,z+.025),color=(.33,.36,.33)))
    lamp.include('white diffuser',rod(radius=r*.91,length=.022,center=(x,y,z-.025),color=(.95,.96,.84)))
    scene.include(f'ceiling pendant {i}',lamp)

# Audit: positive finite dimensions, distinct rod/path points, unique include keys.
# All visible assets include supports before realization; no external resources.
realize(scene)
set_view(CAM_POS,CAM_TARGET,lens=LENS,sensor=36)
world=bpy.data.worlds.new('Dim compartment ambient')
bpy.context.scene.world=world
world.use_nodes=True
world.node_tree.nodes['Background'].inputs[0].default_value=(.36,.37,.30,1)
world.node_tree.nodes['Background'].inputs[1].default_value=.32
area_emitter((-.65,-1.10,2.84),power=150,size=.70,target=(-.7,-.4,.1),color=(.93,.96,1.0))
area_emitter((-.38,1.62,2.77),power=105,size=.65,target=(0,2.3,.4),color=(.93,.97,1.0))
area_emitter((.10,3.50,2.75),power=90,size=.60,target=(0,3.8,.5),color=(.98,1.0,.91))
area_emitter((.15,-3.3,2.7),power=65,size=3,target=(0,1,1.1),color=(1.0,.83,.65))
# Isolate diffuser emission locally beneath its semantic parent.
for i in range(3):
    root=bpy.data.objects.get(f'ceiling pendant {i}')
    if root:
        for obj in root.children_recursive:
            if obj.type=='MESH':
                for slot in obj.material_slots:
                    if slot.material:
                        slot.material=slot.material.copy()
                        slot.material.use_nodes=True
                        bsdf=slot.material.node_tree.nodes.get('Principled BSDF')
                        if bsdf:
                            col=bsdf.inputs['Base Color'].default_value
                            if min(col[:3])>.7:
                                bsdf.inputs['Emission Color'].default_value=(.84,.90,1,1)
                                bsdf.inputs['Emission Strength'].default_value=2.5
scene_bpy=bpy.context.scene
scene_bpy.render.resolution_x=384
scene_bpy.render.resolution_y=512
scene_bpy.render.resolution_percentage=100
scene_bpy.view_settings.view_transform='AgX'
```
